newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia enacts regional retail restrictions.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia enacts regional retail restrictions.

text.p: Indonesia has issued a decree barring retail chains from opening new stores in towns below the level of provincial capitals in a bid to promote small and medium traders, the Jakarta Post reported on Saturday.

Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said while announcing the decree, which was ordered last month by President Suharto, that existing retail chains in regional towns were required to establish partnerships with small and medium retailers, the newspaper reported.

"Big retailers, however, can still set up in areas outside provincial capitals which have very high economic growth, but they will need special licences from the ministers of home affairs and industry and trade," Ariwibowo said.
The newspaper did not say when the decree was signed, but said it was a joint regulation signed by both Ariwibowo and Home Affairs Minister Yogie Memet.
"A joint task force will be set up soon to work out technical details for implementing the joint decree," Ariwibowo said.
Partnerships could be either sub-contracting arrangements for consignment or rental space in department stores and modern shopping centres for small firms, he said.
The plan to restrict large retailers outside the provincial capitals was raised after the first cabinet session on the alleviation of poverty last month.
Analysts say large retailers accounted for 85 percent of total retail sales in 1995.
Indonesia's large retailers include Matahari, Ramayana and Hero Supermarket.
"We believe that the effect for big retailers is not as negative as some felt when the ban was first announced," brokerage Asia Equity said in a report recently.

"The new regulation may result in a slowdown in expansion on (the main island of) Java, but...opening stores outside Java reduces rental and setting up costs which will boost overall productivity," the brokerage said in a column carried by Reuters earlier this month.
